title: The Skull
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: Can you name the glowing skull bone?
Look at the side of the skull.
Which bone is it?
It sits at the side of the head, around the ear.
Your jaw hinges on it, just in front of your ear.
It's D. The temporal bone.
Why it matters: it protects your inner ear, for hearing and balance.

title: The Skull
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: Only one skull bone really moves. Can you name it?
It's the bone that's glowing.
Which bone is it?
The maxilla holds your upper teeth, and it doesn't move.
This bone holds the lower teeth and hinges to open your mouth.
It's B. The mandible.
Why it matters: it's the largest, strongest bone in your face.

title: The Skull
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: You can feel this bone right now. Name it.
Watch the small bone that's glowing.
Which bone is it?
It's not the maxilla, which holds your upper teeth.
This one forms the bump of your cheek.
It's C. The zygomatic bone, your cheekbone.
Why it matters: it shapes your face and guards your eye socket.

title: The Skull
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: The back of your skull has its own bone. Do you know it?
Watch the glowing bone at the back of the head.
Which bone is glowing?
The parietal bones sit on top. This one is lower.
It also has the big opening where the spinal cord passes through.
It's B. The occipital bone.
Why it matters: it protects the part of the brain that handles vision.

title: The Skull
question: Which bones are glowing?
lines: Put your hand on top of your head. You're touching these bones.
Look at the glowing pair across the top of the head.
Which bones are glowing?
The temporal bones sit lower, around the ears.
It's C. The parietal bones.
Why it matters: they protect the top of the brain and meet at the midline.

title: The Skull
question: Which bone holds the upper teeth?
lines: Smile. Your top teeth are anchored in this bone.
Look at the glowing pair of bones around the upper jaw.
Which bone holds the upper teeth?
The lower teeth sit in the mandible, the only moving skull bone.
It's B. The maxilla, a pair joined at the midline.
Why it matters: they also form most of the roof of your mouth.

title: The Skull
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: Touch your forehead. You can feel this bone right now.
Watch the glowing bone at the front of the skull.
Which bone is glowing?
The parietal bones sit behind it, on top of the head.
It's A. The frontal bone, which forms the forehead.
Why it matters: it protects the front of the brain and the eyes.

title: The Skull
question: Which bone forms the bridge of the nose?
lines: You can pinch this bone between your fingers. Name it.
Watch the small pair of bones at the top of the nose.
Which bone forms the bridge of the nose?
The maxilla frames the sides of the nose and holds the upper teeth.
These two small bones meet in the middle, below the forehead.
It's C. The nasal bones.
Why it matters: below them, the nose is shaped by flexible cartilage.

title: The Skull
question: What are these bones commonly called?
lines: Smile and press the top of your cheek. You can feel this bone.
Watch the pair of bones under the eyes.
What are these bones commonly called?
The jawbone is the mandible, the lower bone that moves.
These bones form the prominent part of your cheeks.
It's B. The cheekbones, or zygomatic bones.
Why it matters: they give the face its shape and anchor chewing muscles.

title: The Skull
question: Which skull bone can move?
lines: Almost every bone in your skull is locked in place. One isn't.
Watch the glowing bone at the bottom of the face.
Which skull bone is the one that moves?
The maxilla holds the upper teeth, but it is fixed to the skull.
This lower jaw swings at joints near your ears.
It's D. The mandible.
Why it matters: it's the skull's only movable bone. It lets you chew.
